display.purpose: The hero headline and one closing statement per page at most.

title.purpose: Section heads, each with one plain muted line under it.

name.purpose: Slop names in rows; the leading row sets 1.9rem to 2.25rem.

numeral.purpose: Ranks, counts, votes, goal totals and every tile glyph, tabular.

label.purpose: Uppercase board captions and column headings, in muted.

lede.purpose: The one paragraph under a page title, max 36rem, muted.

action.purpose: Buttons, nav links, menu items and inline links.

meta.purpose: Bylines, times, counts in rows, hints.

mono.purpose: Code, API tokens, slugs, URL fields and launch numbers only.

shadows.name: popover
shadows.purpose: The account menu, the only element that floats over the page.

shadows.name: input-focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Focus indicator on inputs, paired with a focus-coloured border. Not elevation.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour, border and press transitions on buttons, inputs and links.

motion.name: flap
motion.purpose: A tile glyph dropping into place (rotateX -90deg to 0) once the page is live; never in server markup.

motion.name: flap-stagger
motion.purpose: Delay per tile index, so a row of tiles flips left to right.

motion.name: now-pulse
motion.purpose: The lime now bar on today's tile; the only looping motion. Opacity 1 to 0.35.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion collapses every animation and transition.

narrative.overview:
Slopper is set like the board in a station hall: today's slops are listed, ranked and timed against midnight, and every day a maker ships flips a tile to the drip bang "!" from the logo. The page itself is plain platform-white ground and confident condensed signage; the one dark, physical object on it is the board, a panel of split-flap tiles that carries time and days. Everything else stays out of its way.

Density is a list, not a gallery. Launches are rows divided by hairline rules, with a big tabular rank on the left and the votes on the right, the way departures are read top to bottom. Colour is rationed by meaning: lime is spent only on shipping, gold only on wins, red only on urgency and danger. Surfaces are flat; tint is the only elevation.

The system refuses the launch-site card grid and the old taped-cards-on-plaster costume. No tilted cards, no drop shadows, no outlined buttons.
keyCharacteristics: Cool platform-white ground (light) or green-black ground (dark); one deep green-black ink.
Big Shoulders signage for anything read from across the room; Schibsted Grotesk for anything read up close.
The board: dark split-flap tiles for clocks and goal days, dark in both themes.
Lime means shipped, gold means won, red means hurry or danger.
Rows and hairlines instead of cards; flat tinted panels instead of shadows.
The drip bang "!" is the shipped glyph everywhere: logo, goal days, empty covers, favicon.

rules.name: The Shipping Lime Rule
rules.body: Lime is spent only on shipping: shipped days, the primary action, "now" and the current place in navigation. It never decorates a heading, a border or a background panel.

rules.name: The Gold Means Won Rule
rules.body: Gold appears only for a win (slop of the day, slopcessful). A surface with no winner on it has no gold.

rules.name: The Board Stays Dark Rule
rules.body: The board and its tiles are dark in both themes, like the real thing. They never invert with the page.

rules.name: The Token Not Hex Rule
rules.body: Components use the custom properties, never literal hexes, so dark mode is a token swap. The one exception is the gold button's text, which stays #161a13 in both themes because gold stays bright.

rules.name: The Signage Rule
rules.body: Big Shoulders sets anything read from across the room (headings, names, ranks, counts, tiles, captions). Schibsted Grotesk sets everything read up close. Mono is only for code and data codes, never for labels or headings.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number that can change (ranks, votes, clocks, goal counts) uses tabular figures so the board never shifts as it updates.

rules.name: The Tint Is Elevation Rule
rules.body: A grouped area is a flat `sunk` panel. If it needs to stand out more, it becomes the board or takes a tint (gold, red), never a shadow. The popover is the single exception.

dos: Do spend lime only on shipping: shipped days, the one primary action, "now" and the active nav bar.
Do keep gold for wins and red for the last hour, NSFW, errors and destructive zones.
Do put clocks, goal days and short codes on board tiles, label every clock with its zone, and give screen readers the value as text.
Do set lists as rows divided by `line` hairlines, with tabular ranks and counts in Big Shoulders.
Do use a flat `sunk` panel to group controls, and `slop-text` (not raw lime) when lime has to be text on the ground.
Do keep every target at least 2.75rem (44px) and respect reduced motion.
donts: Don't lay launches out as a card grid or as taped, tilted cards on a textured wall.
Don't add drop shadows; the account menu popover is the only one.
Don't outline buttons or tags; they are solid fills or tints.
Don't invert the board or its tiles to light in the light theme.
Don't use Atkinson Hyperlegible Mono for labels, headings or numbers that are not code or data codes.
Don't use emoji as icons or decoration; the drawn icon set and the drip bang carry every glyph.
Don't use kitchen, cooking, restaurant or food imagery anywhere.
